title: Integral rho tensor squares have a free rank-one invariant module
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and algebraically closed residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams over this base. Suppose $H$ is split semisimple simply connected: its geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, every central isogeny onto such a fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism, and choose a split maximal torus $T\subseteq H$ and a Borel subgroup scheme $B\supseteq T$. Here a central isogeny is a surjective group homomorphism with finite central kernel; solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups eventually become trivial; a split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; maximal tori and Borel subgroup schemes have, on each geometric fibre, a maximal torus and a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, respectively. Write $\mathbf G_m(C)=C^\times$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$. A character is a homomorphism of group schemes to $\mathbf G_m$. Let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots determined by $B$, namely the nonzero characters occurring in the adjoint $T$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$; the latter is the tangent module at the identity, defined by dual-number points reducing to the identity. In the character lattice $X^*(T)$, addition means multiplication of character values. Use the rational section modules of [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], with the following explicit description. Let $\rho\in X^*(T)$ satisfy $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$, and let $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ extend $\rho$ and be trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$. This radical is the subgroup whose geometric fibres are the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroups; unipotent means that all geometric points become unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. For every integer $m\ge1$, put $$W_m=\{f\in A[H]:f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^m f(g)\text{ for all commutative }A\text{-algebras }C,\ g\in H(C),\ b\in B(C)\}.$$ Evaluation of $f$ means pullback of the regular function along its $C$-point. Use the left-translation action $(h f)(g)=f(h^{-1}g)$. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with an $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ is the coordinate Hopf algebra. Its invariants are $M^H=\{x:\rho_M(x)=x\otimes1\}$. Equivariant maps commute with coactions; tensor products have diagonal coaction. These identities are tested after every commutative $A$-algebra extension, not just on $A$-points. For every integer $m\ge1$, the invariant $A$-module $(W_m\otimes_A W_m)^H$ is free of rank one, that is, it is isomorphic as an $A$-module to $A$.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(1) and Remark 9.7.3, printed pp.526--527; Seshadri Property I(a) and Lemma 3. This is the integral invariant module, not an assertion that formation of invariants commutes with reduction. Local PDF WANTED; primary published PDF and arXiv HTML read online.

proof.text: Fix $m\ge1$, put $W=W_m$ and $N=W\otimes_AW$. By [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], $W$ is a finite free rational $H$-module of positive rank. If $(e_i)$ is a finite basis of $W$, the tensors $e_i\otimes e_j$ form a basis of $N$: the coefficient functionals $e_i^*\otimes e_j^*$ give the inverse coordinate map. In particular, $N$ embeds in $N\otimes_AK$, where $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, by its coordinates. Choose an algebraic closure $F$ of $K$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure].

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(1) and Remark 9.7.3, printed pp.526--527; primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf. Agent-written flat-kernel and principal-ideal assembly from the existing algebraically closed field case.

proof.text: The functor $M\mapsto M\otimes_AF$ preserves kernels. Let $u:M\to P$ be $A$-linear, so $0\to\ker u\to M\xrightarrow{u}P$ is exact. First, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ is the localization of $A$ at $A\setminus\{0\}$, hence a flat $A$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]; the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] makes $0\to(\ker u)\otimes_AK\to M\otimes_AK\to P\otimes_AK$ exact, i.e. identifies $(\ker u)\otimes_AK$ with $\ker(u\otimes_AK)$. Next $F$ is flat over the field $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], and the same clause of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] over $K$ identifies the kernel after tensoring with $F$. The tensor associator $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$, with inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$, identifies this composite with tensoring over $A$ with $F$. This argument needs no finite generation of $M$ or $P$.

source.place: Tag 00HD, lemma-flat; localization exactness as in the cited node. Apply to the kernel/image and image/cokernel short exact sequences; field modules are free, Tag 09FN.

proof.text: Put $C=A[H]$ and $D=A[B]$, and let $t\in D^\times$ be the character function $\widetilde\rho$. Pullback by right multiplication gives $r:C\to C\otimes_AD$. Define $u:C\to C\otimes_AD$ by $u(f)=r(f)-f\otimes t^m$. Then $W=\ker u$: evaluate this identity at $(g,b)$, and conversely test the pointwise identity on the universal pair with coefficient algebra $C\otimes_AD$. The affine coordinate identifications used here follow from [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the identification $\operatorname{Spec}C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}D\cong\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_AD)$ (and likewise for the base change to $\operatorname{Spec}F$) of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]: homomorphisms $C\otimes_AD\to E$ are exactly compatible pairs of homomorphisms $C,D\to E$. The same description gives $F[H_F]=C\otimes_AF$ and $F[B_F]=D\otimes_AF$, with all multiplication and character maps obtained by scalar extension. By Step 2, $W\otimes_AF$ therefore identifies with the actual regular-function module $W_m(H_F,B_F)$, with exactly the right-character sign in the statement. This identification intertwines left translation: $f(h^{-1}g)$ is the same formula on both sides, tested after every $F$-algebra extension.

proof.text: Let $L=N^H=\ker\delta$, where $\delta:N\to N\otimes_AC$ is $x\mapsto c_N(x)-x\otimes1$ and $c_N$ is the diagonal coaction. Step 2, applied to $\delta$, identifies $L\otimes_AF$ with $(N\otimes_AF)^{H_F}$. Step 3 and the tensor associator identify $N\otimes_AF$ equivariantly with $W_m(H_F,B_F)\otimes_FW_m(H_F,B_F)$. The geometric generic fibre $H_F$ is semisimple simply connected by the geometric-fibre hypotheses on $H$; $T_F,B_F$ are its chosen split maximal torus and Borel, and the character, positive roots and extension are the base changes of the given ones. Thus [lem-sfb-rho-tensor-square-invariant-line] applies over the algebraically closed field $F$ and gives $\dim_F(L\otimes_AF)=1$. Consequently the $K$-subspace $L\otimes_AK\subseteq N\otimes_AK$ has dimension one: extend a basis over $K$ to $F$ and compare dimensions. In particular $L\ne0$.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(1) and Remark 9.7.3, printed pp.526--527; primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf. Agent-written flat-kernel and principal-ideal assembly from the existing algebraically closed field case.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $N$ and a coordinate $j$ nonzero on $L\otimes_AK$. Its restriction to this one-dimensional $K$-space is injective. The image $I=\{x_j:x\in L\}$ is a nonzero ideal of $A$. Every ideal is principal by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so $I=aA$ for some $a\ne0$; choose $x\in L$ with $x_j=a$. For any $y\in L$ write $y_j=ba$ with $b\in A$. Then $y-bx$ has coordinate $j$ equal to zero and hence is zero in $N\otimes_AK$, by injectivity of that coordinate on $L\otimes_AK$. The coordinate embedding of Step 1 implies $y=bx$ already in $N$. Thus $L=Ax$. If $bx=0$, coordinate $j$ gives $ba=0$ and the domain property of $A$ gives $b=0$. Therefore $A\to L$, $b\mapsto bx$, is an $A$-linear isomorphism, as required.
